# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

An IntelliJ Platform plugin ("Codeowls") that adds first-class editor support for `CODEOWNERS` files (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket). It registers a `CODEOWNERS` language for any file literally named `CODEOWNERS`. Despite the template README describing Kotlin, **all production and test code is Java** under `src/main/java` and `src/test/java`.

## Commands

- Build: `./gradlew build`
- Run all tests: `./gradlew test`
- Run one test class: `./gradlew test --tests 'net.wolfig.codeowls.matcher.CodeownersGlobTest'`
- Run one test method: `./gradlew test --tests 'net.wolfig.codeowls.matcher.CodeownersGlobTest.methodName'`
- Launch a sandbox IDE with the plugin: `./gradlew runIde`
- Verify plugin compatibility against target IDEs: `./gradlew verifyPlugin`

The IntelliJ Platform SDK and target IDE (`intellijIdea("2025.3.5")`) are pulled by the `org.jetbrains.intellij.platform` Gradle plugin; the first build downloads a large SDK. `.run/` holds equivalent IDE run configurations (Run Plugin, Run Tests, Run Verifications).

Note: the user runs tests themselves — do not auto-run `./gradlew test` to verify changes unless asked.

## Architecture

Everything keys off one shared, handwritten lexer. There is **no PSI tree / parser** in the usual sense — `CodeownersParserDefinition` exists to register the file type and highlighting, but semantic work is done by re-lexing text directly. When changing token semantics, the lexer is the single source of truth and most other components consume its output.

Layers, bottom-up:

- **`lexer/`** — `CodeownersLexer` (extends `LexerBase`) is a stateful, line-oriented lexer. Every line is classified as empty / comment / GitLab section header (`[Name]`, `^[Name]`, with optional `[N]` approval count and default owners) / rule (`pattern owner...`). Token categories live in `CodeownersTokenTypes`. Both syntax highlighting and rule parsing drive this same lexer.

- **`matcher/`** — the ownership model, IDE-independent and the most heavily unit-tested code.
  - `CodeownersRuleParser.parse()` is the **only** place lexer tokens become the rule model. It applies GitLab section semantics: a section header's default owners and approval count are inherited by rules in that section that name no owners of their own; a rule's own owners override. The owners stored on each `CodeownersRule` are the *effective* owners after inheritance.
  - `CodeownersGlob.compile()` turns a CODEOWNERS glob into an anchored regex over forward-slash, project-relative paths. Semantics follow GitHub's documented rules (a subset of gitignore) — see its Javadoc before touching `*`/`**`/`?`/anchoring behavior. Leading `!` (GitLab negation) is stripped here; callers handle negation. Resolution is **last-match-wins**.

- **`statusbar/CodeownersService`** — project-level `@Service` that locates the active CODEOWNERS file by walking a file's parent chain trying `CANDIDATE_PATHS` (`.github/CODEOWNERS`, `CODEOWNERS`, `docs/CODEOWNERS`, `.gitlab/CODEOWNERS`, in that precedence), parses it (cached by modification stamp), and resolves the matching rule. It is intentionally **listener-free**: it reparses lazily on stamp change; the status bar widget owns the VFS/PSI listeners and drives re-resolution to avoid a service↔UI feedback loop.

- **Feature packages** (each roughly one `plugin.xml` extension): `highlighting/` (syntax + color settings page), `folding/` (GitLab section blocks), `completion/` (path, owner, and section-name completion; owners come from the file, Git-history contributors, and built-in GitLab roles `@@developer`/`@@maintainer`/`@@owner`), `inlay/` ("N files" hints + toggle action), `navigation/` (gutter line marker for matched files, Ctrl/Cmd+Click owner → GitHub/GitLab page resolved from the Git remote), `inspection/` (flags rules matching no file or shadowed by a later rule, with quick fix), `refactoring/` (rewrites rule paths on file move/rename), `suggestion/` (confidence-ranked owner suggestions for un-owned files).

All extension points are wired in `src/main/resources/META-INF/plugin.xml`; user-facing strings live in `messages/CodeownersBundle.properties`.

## Tests

- Framework is **JUnit 4** (`@Test`/`@Before`/`@After`, not JUnit 5). Tests follow Arrange / Act / Assert.
- Pure-logic tests (`matcher/`, lexer) run standalone. Anything touching PSI, completion, editor actions, or project services uses the IntelliJ `CodeInsightTestFixture`.
- **Fixture setup must go through `IdeaTestFixtureFactory.createCodeInsightFixture(builder.getFixture())`** (built from `createLightFixtureBuilder`) — not a bare `IdeaProjectTestFixture`. Some fixture operations must run on the EDT (see existing tests' use of `EdtTestUtil`). Copy the setUp/tearDown pattern from an existing fixture test (e.g. `CodeownersCompletionTest`) when adding one.
- Configure content with `fixture.configureByText(CodeownersFileType.INSTANCE, ...)`; `<caret>` markers in the text drive completion/caret-position assertions.

Implement a new CodeOwls feature called **"Explain Ownership"**.

## Goal

Users should be able to understand **why a specific project file has its effective CODEOWNERS owner(s)**.

For a selected project file, CodeOwls should show:

* the effective owner(s)
* the effective required approval count, if applicable
* all CODEOWNERS rules that match the file
* which rule ultimately wins
* inherited GitLab section owners / approval counts, where relevant
* the CODEOWNERS file and line number for each matching rule
* a convenient way to navigate to the winning or matching rule

Example output:

```text
src/payment/PaymentService.java

Effective owners:
@payment-team

Required approvals:
2

Matching rules:

✓ /src/**                  @developers
✓ /src/payment/**          @backend
✓ /src/payment/*.java      @payment-team   ← effective rule
```

If GitLab section inheritance applies, make that visible as well, for example:

```text
[Backend][2] @backend-team

/src/payment/**
```

should explain that the rule inherits:

```text
Owners: @backend-team
Required approvals: 2
```

## Entry Point

Add an action called:

**Explain CODEOWNERS Ownership**

The action should be available from an appropriate JetBrains context, preferably:

* Project View context menu for files
* Editor context menu when an actual project file is open
* optionally Find Action / Search Everywhere

Do not offer the action for the CODEOWNERS file itself unless it makes sense with the existing architecture.

## UI

Use a native JetBrains UI component.

Prefer a lightweight popup if the information fits well there.

The popup should contain:

1. selected file path
2. effective owners
3. required approval count, if any
4. matching rules in CODEOWNERS evaluation order
5. clear indication of the effective/winning rule

Each matching rule should ideally be clickable so that the user can jump directly to the corresponding line in the CODEOWNERS file.

If no rule matches, show something like:

```text
No matching CODEOWNERS rule found.

This file currently has no CODEOWNERS owner.
```

If an existing fallback/default ownership mechanism exists in CodeOwls, explain that state accurately instead of inventing CODEOWNERS semantics.

## Important Semantics

Reuse the **existing CodeOwls CODEOWNERS parsing and matching logic**.

Do not implement a second independent glob matcher or CODEOWNERS evaluator.

The explanation must produce exactly the same effective ownership result as:

* the existing status bar widget
* existing owner lookup logic
* GitLab section inheritance
* GitLab approval count handling
* negated GitLab patterns
* rule precedence / last matching rule semantics

Before implementing, inspect the existing codebase and identify:

* CODEOWNERS parser/model classes
* glob matching implementation
* ownership resolution logic
* status bar widget implementation
* GitLab section handling
* navigation utilities for CODEOWNERS rules

Refactor shared logic if needed rather than duplicating ownership calculation.

## Suggested Internal Model

If useful, introduce a reusable ownership explanation/result model similar to:

```java
OwnershipExplanation
- VirtualFile targetFile
- List<MatchedRule> matchedRules
- EffectiveOwnership effectiveOwnership
```

and:

```java
MatchedRule
- rule
- sourceFile
- line / text range
- resolvedOwners
- approvalCount
- inheritedFromSection
- effective
```

The exact structure should follow the existing CodeOwls architecture and naming conventions.

The important part is that the ownership resolver can return not only the final owner, but also the **evaluation trace** explaining how that result was reached.

## Architecture

Prefer something conceptually similar to:

```text
CODEOWNERS
    ↓
Parser
    ↓
Ownership Resolver
    ├── resolve(file)
    └── explain(file)
            ↓
      OwnershipExplanation
```

`resolve(file)` and `explain(file)` should share the same evaluation logic so that they cannot drift apart.

Do not break existing APIs unless necessary.

## Performance

The feature should be responsive for normal repositories.

Do not scan the entire repository just to explain one file.

Only evaluate the relevant CODEOWNERS rules against the selected file.

Reuse existing caches/indexes/services where available.

Avoid blocking the EDT with expensive work.

Follow JetBrains threading requirements used elsewhere in the plugin.

## Navigation

Clicking a matching rule should navigate to the exact corresponding CODEOWNERS rule.

Reuse existing PSI / VirtualFile / navigation utilities where possible.

If line numbers are currently derived manually, prefer stable PSI/text range references if the existing parser supports them.

## Testing

Add tests covering at least:

1. one matching rule
2. multiple matching rules where the last one wins
3. file with no matching rule
4. multiple owners
5. GitLab section default owners
6. GitLab section approval count
7. explicit rule owners overriding section owners
8. GitLab optional section
9. GitLab negation pattern if supported by the existing matcher
10. navigation/source information being associated with the correct rule

Also make sure existing ownership-resolution tests continue to pass.

## Implementation Process

First inspect the repository and explain briefly which existing classes are responsible for:

* parsing
* matching
* ownership resolution
* status bar ownership display
* GitLab sections

Then implement the feature following the existing project structure and coding conventions.

Avoid unnecessary abstractions or large unrelated refactorings.

After implementation:

* run the relevant tests
* run the project's normal verification/build task
* fix any introduced warnings or failures
* summarize the changed files and architectural decisions

## Acceptance Criteria

The feature is complete when:

* I can select a project file and invoke **Explain CODEOWNERS Ownership**
* I can see all CODEOWNERS rules matching that file
* I can clearly identify the effective rule
* effective owners match the existing CodeOwls owner resolution
* GitLab section inheritance is explained correctly
* approval counts are displayed correctly
* matching rules can be navigated to in CODEOWNERS
* files without an owner are handled gracefully
* existing CodeOwls behavior remains unchanged
* automated tests cover the explanation logic

net.wolfig.codeowls Codeowls johannes CODEOWNERS files used by GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket.

Features
  • Syntax highlighting for comments, glob patterns (including GitLab negation !/config/**/*.rb), user / team / role / e-mail owners, GitLab section headers, optional sections, and approval counts — colors configurable under Settings → Editor → Color Scheme → CODEOWNERS.
  • Status bar widget showing the owners (and any required approval count) of the currently selected file; click to jump to the matching rule — or, when the file has no specific owner, to get confidence-ranked owner suggestions you can add to CODEOWNERS in one click.
  • GitLab section support — rules inherit their section's default owners ([Documentation] @docs-team) and approval count; a rule's own owners override the default.
  • Inlay hints displaying the number of files each glob rule matches in the current project; toggle via Find Action → Toggle CODEOWNERS File Count Hints.
  • Matched-file navigation — a gutter icon on each wildcard / directory rule lists the project files it matches; pick one to jump to it.
  • Path completion for glob patterns and section-name completion for GitLab [Section] headers already used in the file.
  • Owner completion drawn from owners already in the file, Git-history contributors, and the built-in GitLab roles (@@developer, @@maintainer, @@owner).
  • Owner navigation — Ctrl/Cmd+Click a user or team owner to open their GitHub / GitLab page (resolved from the repository's Git remote) in the browser.
  • Move / rename sync — rules pointing at a moved or renamed file or directory are rewritten to the new path automatically.
  • Inspections that warn about unnecessary rules — patterns matching no project file, and rules fully shadowed by a later rule — with a quick fix to remove them.
  • Code folding for GitLab section blocks.
Matches any file literally named CODEOWNERS — including .github/CODEOWNERS, .gitlab/CODEOWNERS, docs/CODEOWNERS, and a repository-root CODEOWNERS. ]]> com.intellij.modules.platform
